{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Free Press Foundation (FPF, Mongolian: “Чөлөөт хэвлэл сан” сонины хэвлэх үйлдвэр ) is one of the largest printing houses in Mongolia.","title":"Free Press Foundation"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It was first established in 1996 under the name Newspaper Printing House with a grant aid from the Danish International Development Assistance Agency within the framework of the project “Free and Independent Press in Mongolia” implemented in accordance with the agreement between the Government of Mongolia and the Government of Denmark.","title":"Free Press Foundation"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The Government of Denmark commemorated the Free Press Foundation to the transition to free democratic society system and free open economic market in Mongolia.","title":"Free Press Foundation"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Between 1996-2005, the Free Press Foundation printed up to 90% of total number of newspaper titles in Mongolia.","title":"Free Press Foundation"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" Presently, it prints over 60% of total number of newspaper titles and over 70% of total circulation of nationally printed newspapers.","title":"Free Press Foundation"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Rossendale Free Press is a weekly newspaper published in Rossendale, Lancashire, England and distributed in Rossendale's four main towns of Rawtenstall, Bacup, Haslingden, and Ramsbottom.","title":"Rossendale Free Press"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It is owned by Manchester Evening News Media, which publishes 19 other newspapers, and its current circulation is 14,369.","title":"Rossendale Free Press"}],"peer_messages":["Unverified peer answer: noanswer"],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"The Rossendale Free Press serves the town how far north of Manchester?"}
